data.title: Oral cephalosporins (cephalexin, cefadroxil, cefuroxime, cefixime, cefpodoxime)
data.summary: Other antibacterials · β-lactam antibiotics — 1st (cephalexin, cefadroxil), 2nd (cefuroxime) and 3rd generation (cefixime, cefpodoxime) oral cephalosporins
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antibacterials_

**Class:** β-lactam antibiotics — 1st (cephalexin, cefadroxil), 2nd (cefuroxime) and 3rd generation (cefixime, cefpodoxime) oral cephalosporins

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibit cell-wall synthesis (PBP binding) → bactericidal
- Moving from 1st to 3rd generation: less Gram-positive (staph) activity, more Gram-negative activity and β-lactamase stability

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- 1st generation (cephalexin, cefadroxil): staphylococcal and streptococcal skin infections — impetigo, cellulitis, furunculosis, infected eczema, wound infection
- 2nd generation (cefuroxime axetil): early Lyme disease (alternative to doxycycline), skin infections
- 3rd generation: cefixime 400 mg single dose (NACO grey and yellow kits — gonorrhoea/cervicitis, PID); cefpodoxime for skin and soft-tissue infections
- Injectable 3rd generation (ceftriaxone): see exam-list post

## Dose & formulations
- Cephalexin 500 mg four times daily (25–50 mg/kg/day in children)
- Cefadroxil 500 mg–1 g twice daily
- Cefuroxime axetil 500 mg twice daily (Lyme 14–21 days)
- Cefixime 400 mg single dose (gonorrhoea, as per NACO kit); 200 mg twice daily for other infections
- Cefpodoxime 200 mg twice daily

## Adverse effects
- Diarrhoea, C. difficile colitis
- Hypersensitivity — cross-reactivity with penicillin is low (about 1–2%), mainly with similar side chains (cephalexin/cefadroxil share amoxicillin's side chain)
- Serum-sickness-like reaction (classically cefaclor in children)
- Positive Coombs test, rarely haemolytic anaemia

## Contraindications
- Previous anaphylaxis to a cephalosporin; caution in immediate penicillin allergy

## Drug interactions
- Probenecid raises levels; alcohol (some injectables with MTT side chain — disulfiram-like)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding.

## Viva points
- Generations and their spectrum shift
- Cefixime is the oral drug in NACO kits
- Low cross-reactivity with penicillin — related to side chains

_Sources: Khopkar ch.1 (Cephalosporins); Wolverton 4e ch.9; NACO STI guidelines. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
